item.title: Canada Is Investigating Skyrim Username Error That Sent Innocent Man to Prison
item.description:
Nova Scotia officials are examining how a mistaken username inspired by The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim helped send an innocent man to prison for 18 months. The case is now drawing scrutiny over how a seemingly minor error went undetected through multiple stages of the Canadian justice system, resulting in what a top government official labeled a "shocking miscarriage of justice" for one unfortunate Skyrim fan.

Brandon Klayme spent 18 months in prison due to a Skyrim username mix-up resulting in a 2023 conviction on three charges related to the possession of child abuse material, all of which were tied to online communications with a 12-year-old girl from Wisconsin. The case hinged on investigators linking Klayme to a Kik account used in the offenses. On July 23, 2026, the Nova Scotia Court of Appeal acquitted him on all counts after new evidence showed that investigators had mistaken one nearly identical username for another, with the court declaring Klayme "factually innocent."

Insider Clarifies Elder Scrolls 6 Timeline After Bethesda Layoffs

An established Xbox insider clarifies how recent layoffs at Bethesda affect the development timeline for The Elder Scrolls 6.

By Dominik Bošnjak

Nova Scotia Wants Answers After the Skyrim Username Mix-Up

Nova Scotia Attorney General Scott Armstrong has now requested a detailed briefing from the province's Public Prosecution Service on the steps taken throughout Klayme's case. Armstrong said he wants to understand how the error passed through the justice system before deciding what action to take, adding that the province must also determine how to prevent a similar wrongful conviction from happening again. "I'm very concerned about this," the Attorney General said on August 6, CBC reports.

Armstrong has not ruled out a public inquiry and said he would be willing to meet with Klayme or his representatives, though no discussions about potential compensation have taken place yet. The unfortunate Skyrim fan's case has also prompted calls for action from opposition politicians. Nova Scotia NDP Leader Claudia Chender described it as a "shocking miscarriage of justice," while Liberal House Leader Derek Mombourquette opined that the circumstances surrounding the wrongful conviction constitute grounds for a public inquiry.

How the Skyrim Username Mix-Up Led Investigators to Klayme

Investigators were trying to identify the Kik user "fus__ro_dah," with two underscores between "fus" and "ro." Klayme's account, "fus_ro_dah," used only one. Both names reference Skyrim 's famous Fus Ro Dah Dragon Shout, but Wisconsin police mistakenly requested subscriber information for Klayme's account instead of the one involved in the offenses. The request returned Klayme's email address, which investigators used to obtain Google records linking him to a Halifax IP address. Halifax Regional Police then searched his home on February 5, 2021, and seized several phones and laptops.

Elder Scrolls Fan Spots a Cat Named M'aiq the Liar at a Pet Store
Skyblivion Reveals New Screenshots and Gets Encouraging Development Update

Court Records Show There Was No Digital Evidence Linking Klayme to the Offenses

The Court of Appeal judgment adds another striking detail to the case: when Halifax Regional Police searched Klayme's residence and seized phones and laptops, investigators found no evidence linking him to the victim, the Kik conversations, or the intimate images exchanged with the actual offender. The court also noted that there was no activity on Klayme's Kik account during the period of the offenses and that Kik is a standalone entity that operates independently of and is in no way affiliated with Google. Likewise, the presiding appellate judge panel found no evidence that his Google account had been used to communicate with the victim. The unusual username at the center of the case derives from Skyrim 's Dragon Language, in which "Fus Ro Dah" is the game's Unrelenting Force Shout.

item.title: New Steam Game Has Serious Kingdom Hearts Vibes
item.description:
Expectations are undoubtedly high for Kingdom Hearts 4 , because as the start of a new saga, it’s poised to be a healthy jumping-on point for fans and a chance to tell a less convoluted story. The realistic, more mature setting of Quadratum not only represents Sora’s aging, but opens the door to more Final Fantasy representation and less cartoony Disney worlds like Marvel and Star Wars. Still, with the June 2026 trailer lacking even a release window — and showing no Disney locations whatsoever — it feels like the game is still several months away from release. And if that’s the case, Kingdom Hearts fans may want to consider exploring Steam for some alternatives, as there’s only so many times one can replay older KH titles before wanting something new.

One upcoming Steam game that should look incredibly appealing to fans of the Kingdom Hearts franchise is Luminous Nights . While its name forms a connection to one of its key inspirations — the fairytale 1001 Arabian Nights — its mechanics are undoubtedly inspired by Square Enix and Disney’s beloved collaboration. And given how crucial fairytales like Arabian Nights have been to establishing the Disney brand, the similar vibe goes beyond just gameplay. From the HUD to the character models, Luminous Nights is unashamedly a Kingdom Hearts -like, but that’s exactly what many players likely need right now.

Given the 2027 release window on Luminous Nights ’ Steam page, the game launching before KH4 feels likely.

New Co-Op Game on Steam is Hogwarts Legacy Meets It Takes Two

An intriguing co-op game on Steam flew under the radar, but its very positive reviews suggest it successfully merges It Takes Two and Hogwarts Legacy.

1
By Richard Warren

Luminous Nights Features at a Glance

  • ATTACK with swords and magic through an action RPG gameplay system.
  • EXPLORE a handcrafted 3D environment and use platforming abilities to reach hidden loot.
  • LEVEL UP the more you play, expanding the ability pool of protagonist Faris.
  • MEET a range of memorable characters, from a sneaky figure in a basket to genie-like guards.

Master fast-paced melee combat and powerful magic, unlock new abilities and weapons, explore the mystical city of Noor through 3D platforming, and rally memorable allies against the Masked King.

Luminous Nights is Basically a Super Fleshed Out Version of Kingdom Hearts’ Agrabah

If one were to imagine an entire Kingdom Hearts game set within Aladdin ’s world, the result would likely look a whole lot like Luminous Nights . In this game, players take control of a boy named Faris as he strives to free his home from an endless night. On his journey to defeat a corrupt masked tyrant, Faris will encounter evil jinn, but also helpful NPCs that will require assistance. While these characters may not be instantly recognizable like Jasmine, Iago, and so on, they do have distinct designs and personalities, which should make completing their quests entertaining.

Much like Kingdom Hearts , though, Luminous Nights looks like it will be incredibly fun even if players aren’t taking in the story. This is largely because of its fast-paced action combat, which sees players slicing through enemies with melee weapons while also mixing in a bit of magic whenever they see fit. Just like Kingdom Hearts , while players will spend a good deal of time dodging, parrying, and doing aerial combos, they’ll also be able to mix in lightning, ice, and so on. Classic healing spells and deflect are available, too, as is a flare option, allowing players to string together impressive combos and make Faris look like a Keyblade wielder.

However, though the combat and progression are a key part of the game’s DNA — like all true RPGs, players level up to acquire new abilities for their character — the world is similarly important. Developer Yahya Danboos has put great care into capturing Middle Eastern architecture and folklore within the game’s setting. Players can expect to platform across markets and palaces, clear dungeons, and so on. And as they do, they should keep their eyes peeled for chests with useful gear items for Faris, from weaponry to outfits. For fans of the long-running Kingdom Hearts series, it’s hard to imagine a better alternative than this 2027 release.

item.title: Highly Rated 2026 Co-Op Horror Game Shadow Drops DLC
item.description:
Co-op horror game fans have a new release to playthrough right now, as Reanimal has shadow-dropped its first story DLC. Reanimal initially released back in February from the original developers of Little Nightmares 1 and 2 , quickly becoming one of the best horror games of the year. Players looking to continue the story of Reanimal can jump into The Prisoner DLC right now, with two more DLCs planned to launch in the coming months.

2026 has already been a massive year for horror game fans, with major titles like Resident Evil Requiem and Directive 8020 releasing. Reanimal offers a different type of horror experience for fans of co-op games, since players must work together with a friend to overcome the nightmarish world the game throws them into. With a score of 80 on OpenCritic, Reanimal marks one of the strongest showings of the horror genre so far this year, and The Prisoner DLC only enhances the experience.

New Steam Co-Op Horror Party Game is Already a Hit with 89% Very Positive Reviews

A brand-new co-op horror party game on Steam has launched to very positive reviews, the latest in the genre to blow up on the platform.

By Drew Swanson

Reanimal - The Prisoner DLC is Available Now

Revealed during the THQ Nordic Showcase 2026, The Prisoner debuted as the first story DLC for Reanimal . Features of the DLC include:

  • Two new playable characters
  • Unparalleled atmospheric horror and a terrifying new threat
  • New locations and unexpected twists on familiar places
  • A new chapter in Reanimal ‘s minimalist, interpretive narrative experience

The Prisoner follows two new characters within Reanimal co-op gameplay: the Soldier and the Prisoner, as they fight to survive among the ravages of war. New bosses, such as the Flamethrower Solider, are also part of Reanimal 's new DLC, along with three new Reanimal chapters for players to complete.

Although Reanimal - The Prisoner can be beaten in just a couple of hours, more DLC is on the way for the game in the near future. Following The Prisoner, two more story DLCs are planned for Reanimal :

  • Reanimal DLC 2 — Between October and December 2026
  • Reanimal DCL 3 — Between January and March 2027

The three Reanimal DLCs comprise The Expanded World, which is broken up into these separate chapters. Details beyond release windows for the second and third Reanimal DLCs have not been shared yet.
